items.question: What is the difference between normative political theory and empirical work in political science?
items.answer: The difference between normative political theory and empirical work in political science is that normative political theory focuses on what should happen and how the world should be organized, while empirical work in political science is concerned with how the world is actually organized. Normative political theory tends to develop theories that do not account for the current realities, whereas empirical work uses actual data to analyze political phenomena.
